user_intent: A single wide split-frame image drawing a direct visual parallel between an adult's work environment and a child's learning environment — making the argument that we would never accept for ourselves what we routinely accept for students. Left half: an adult professional in a gray corporate cubicle — fixed chair, gray fabric walls, fluorescent overhead light, isolated, uninspired. Right half: exactly the same camera framing and scale, but an elementary school student at a modern flexible learning space — warm natural light, moveable furniture, engaged and curious. Same human dignity. Completely different environments. The image asks one question without words: why?

subject.description: Adult professional, approximately 35-40 years old, gender-neutral presentation — could read as any adult school administrator or office worker. Wearing a plain button-down shirt in muted gray-blue. Seated in a standard fixed office chair with no flexibility, in a gray fabric cubicle with low walls. Slightly slumped posture, elbow on desk, one hand resting near a keyboard or on the desk surface. Expression tired, distracted, enduring. Eyes looking slightly downward or forward at nothing engaging. The body language communicates constraint, not productivity.
subject.pose: seated in fixed office chair inside gray fabric cubicle walls, one elbow on desk surface, slight slouch, looking forward or slightly downward, not engaged with any task — the posture of someone enduring their environment rather than thriving in it

subject.description: Elementary school student, approximately 10 years old, Latina girl with dark hair in a loose braid, wearing a warm coral long-sleeve shirt and dark pants. Seated at a modern flexible school table — same camera framing and scale as the adult on the left, but the environment around her is completely alive. Leaning slightly forward, both hands resting on or near project materials, head tilted with curiosity, expression engaged and present. Her body language communicates possibility, not endurance.
subject.pose: seated at a modern flexible school table, leaning slightly forward, both hands near project materials on the surface, head tilted with curiosity, body open and engaged — the posture of someone whose environment invites participation

scene.location: Two adjacent environments occupying a single wide frame — a corporate office cubicle on the left and a modern elementary school learning space on the right — shot at the same eye level, same scale, same framing, to make the parallel unavoidable.

lighting.left_half: cold overhead fluorescent office lighting — flat, even, pallid, no warmth or directionality. The light that makes time feel slow.
lighting.right_half: warm natural sunlight from large windows — directional, golden, alive. The light that makes time feel purposeful.

background_elements_left: standard gray fabric cubicle walls, low partition height
basic fixed-height desk surface with no personalization
standard corporate office chair with no flexibility or adjustment
overhead fluorescent tube lighting — cold and flat
generic computer monitor or keyboard on desk surface
muted gray and beige color palette throughout
identical cubicles visible in background, suggesting sameness and scale
no plants, no color, no warmth — purely functional and constraining
background_elements_right: modern flexible school table with warm wood tone surface
moveable upholstered chair in a muted teal or blue
large windows on the right wall with warm natural light streaming in
project materials — paper, markers, small model pieces — on the table surface
open, warm learning environment visible in background
warm wood flooring, clean ceiling, sense of spatial possibility
subtle color in furniture and environment — alive, not institutional
scene.dividing_element: A clean vertical divide at the center of the frame — ideally a wall edge, a column, or a sharp lighting temperature shift from cold fluorescent left to warm natural right. The divide is structural and intentional, not soft or gradual.

composition.framing_note: Both subjects should be framed identically — same distance from camera, same height in frame, same relationship to their work surface. The parallel framing IS the argument. The only difference is the environment around them.
composition.left_half_content: Adult in corporate cubicle — gray, fixed, fluorescent, isolated. Occupies left 50% of frame.
composition.right_half_content: Elementary student at flexible school table — warm, open, natural light, engaged. Occupies right 50% of frame.

logo_safe_zone.instruction: This region falls within the corporate cubicle side of the split frame. Keep human subjects and faces clear of this corner — gray cubicle wall, desk surface, or office floor is acceptable here. Kay-Twelve logo badge overlay applied in post-processing.

negative_prompt: primary subject in bottom left corner
advanced._note: Negative prompts intentionally omit 'artificial light', 'sterile', and 'studio lighting' — the left cubicle half requires fluorescent light, institutional sterility, and corporate constraint as deliberate visual contrast elements.
